name: Utah

agency.name: Utah Labor Commission, Utah Antidiscrimination and Labor Division (UALD)

rates2026.note: Set by Labor Commission rule; by statute it may not exceed the federal minimum wage

minWage.smallEmployer: The Utah Minimum Wage Act does not apply to employees already covered by the federal FLSA; the state rate equals the federal $7.25.

tipped.note: Adults and minors; tips plus base wage must equal at least $7.25

minWage.other: Training wage for workers under 18: $4.25 per hour during the first 90 days of employment, then $7.25.

source.quote: The minimum wage in Utah is $7.25 per hour.

overtime.note: Utah has no overtime law; overtime falls under the federal FLSA (time and a half after 40 hours a week), enforced by the U.S. Department of Labor.

source.quote: There is no Utah overtime law (page directs overtime claims to the U.S. Department of Labor, Fair Labor Standards Act)

sickLeave.note: No statewide paid sick leave requirement.

source.quote: In general, Utah labor law does not require an employer to provide benefits to its employees.

finalPay.fired: within 24 hours of separation (wages due immediately)
finalPay.quit: on the next regular payday (if no written contract for a definite period)
finalPay.ptoNote: No law requires paid leave; if an employer establishes a policy or practice it must follow it.

source.quote: the employer shall pay the wages to the employee within 24 hours of the time of separation at the specified place of payment

ptoSource.quote: If an employer does establish a policy or practice of providing benefits they are expected to abide by the policy or practice in a non-discriminatory manner.

breaks.minorsOnly: Under 18: a 30-minute lunch within the first five hours, and a 10-minute break for each four hours worked (no more than three consecutive hours without a 10-minute break).

source.quote: Employers must provide at least a 30-minute lunch within the first five hours of a minor employee's workday.

rightToWorkSource.quote: whereby membership in such labor union, labor organization or any other type of association is made a condition of employment ... declared illegal

notes.text: Cities, towns and counties may not set a minimum wage above the federal minimum wage, including for their contractors.

source.quote: A city, town, or county may not establish, mandate, or require a minimum wage that exceeds the federal minimum wage

notes.text: A fired employee who is not paid within 24 hours can send a written demand; wages then keep running at the daily rate until paid, up to 60 days.

source.quote: the wages of the employee shall continue from the date of demand until paid, but in no event to exceed 60 days
